title: Tractor-drawn malanga seeder built from a scrapped pipe-cart chassis
summary: A tractor-towed planting machine for malanga (taro) tubers assembled almost entirely from decommissioned parts.
how_it_works: The frame reuses the chassis of a nationally-made pipe-carrying cart, plus chains, pins and the working bodies of a furrower taken from retired machines. A chain-belt fitted with welded scoop attachments (3 cm diameter, 6.5 cm deep, spaced 5 links apart) picks up tubers and drops them into the furrow, while furrowing and covering mechanisms ride on the frame. It works 90 cm wide, plants 10-15 cm deep, and its hoppers hold 50 kg.
problem: Mechanized planting of malanga was needed without access to purpose-built or imported agricultural machinery.
materials: furrower working bodies from retired machines
fabcity_relevance: A canonical example of building agricultural machinery from a salvage bill-of-materials — directly relevant to a fab lab assembling task-specific farm tools from local scrap rather than importing whole machines.

title: Multi-use tractor cultivator with swappable working bodies
title_original: Cultivadora de tractor para uso multiple
summary: A single rugged tractor implement that performs many field tasks by changing its working organs.
how_it_works: The implement cultivates, furrows, prepares soil, cross-cultivates and harrows depending on which working organs are fitted. It has a 2.5 m working width and can work to 12 inches deep. In one day it can cultivate, hill or harrow one caballeria of land (and about half that when breaking new ground), serving crops from plantain and cassava to tomato, pepper and squash.
problem: Many separate field machines were unavailable, so one adaptable implement had to cover multiple tillage tasks.
fabcity_relevance: Modular tool-head swapping on one chassis to replace a shed full of single-purpose machines is a core distributed-manufacturing strategy a fab lab can apply to farm and shop equipment.

title: Ox-drawn three-row grain seeder from recovered parts
title_original: Maquina sembradora de granos por traccion animal
summary: A lightweight ox-drawn precision grain seeder, in use since 1991, built mostly from recovered materials.
how_it_works: Three sections each carry an adjustable articulated furrower, a delivery mechanism with a perforated metering disc, an adjustable two-flap covering cap and an adjustable compaction wheel. A cable-pulley-and-bar suspension lets the operator lift the working organs out of the furrow during transport. Row spacing (70/80/90 cm) and plant spacing are set by swapping disc sets through a simple transmission ratio; the whole rig is pulled by an ox yoke and managed by one seated operator.
problem: Powered, imported seed drills were unavailable and costly, so a low-cost animal-traction seeder was needed.
fabcity_relevance: A precision seeder that swaps cheap metering discs for different crops and runs on animal power shows how to design energy-independent, parts-swappable ag tools — a fit for low-input distributed food production.

title: Low-cost windmill water pump with no bearings or gears
summary: A simple, very low-cost windmill that pumps water while deliberately avoiding hard-to-source bearings and gears.
how_it_works: The design uses no bearings, gears or other hard-to-acquire parts. It consists of a mast, a blade/vane and suction components (check valve, piston, etc.), guyed up with tension stays, with the blades adjusted to suit wind direction and intensity. It extracts water at 0.4 litres per second and handles a head of 70 metres.
problem: Pumping water was needed where bearings, gears and other manufactured drive parts were impossible to obtain.
fabcity_relevance: Designing the bearing and gearbox out of a wind pump to dodge the hardest-to-source parts is exactly the kind of constraint-driven redesign a fab lab uses to make machines locally buildable and repairable.

title: MTZ-80 tractor brake discs cut from worn clutch friction discs
title_original: Recuperacion de discos de freno DEL MTZ-80
summary: Replacement brake discs for the MTZ-80 tractor made by re-cutting the friction material of its clutch discs.
how_it_works: Workers take the friction fibre material of the tractor's clutch disc and punch/cut it following a pattern or die, producing brake discs for the MTZ-80 from that recovered material.
problem: Replacement brake discs for MTZ-80 tractors could not be imported or bought during the shortage.
fabcity_relevance: Harvesting a usable engineered material (friction lining) from one worn part to die-cut another is a concrete materials-recovery pattern for a fab lab keeping vehicles and machines running without a supply chain.

title: Creole cane-harvester cutting blades made by double-edge sharpening
title_original: Segmento de los discos de corte criollos
summary: Locally-made ('criollo') cutting-disc blade segments for sugarcane combines, produced by sharpening both edges to replace scarce Soviet imports.
how_it_works: The technique consists of giving the creole blade segments a cutting edge on both sides, for the segments used in sugarcane combine harvesters. This resolves the shortage of legitimate parts formerly imported from the ex-Soviet Union. Three platoons of combines ran the harvest using these creole blades with good results, and several were produced at MINAZ's Central Workshop of the Complex Brigade in Cienfuegos.
problem: Genuine sugarcane-combine cutting blades imported from the USSR became unavailable after the Soviet collapse.
fabcity_relevance: Re-shoring a critical consumable wear part (harvester blades) in a local workshop when the import line dies is precisely the resilience play a fab lab network offers a city's food system.

title: Hand-operated adjustable aluminum tube cutter
title_original: Maquina para cortar tubos de aluminio
summary: A clamshell hand tool that cuts aluminum tubes of varying diameters with an adjustable circular blade.
how_it_works: The device is two half-shells ('tiles') hinged together; the front shell carries an 8 mm-thick, 40 mm-diameter circular cutting blade whose depth is set by a screw thread according to the tube's circumference. Three 204 ball-bearing boxes let the front shell slide circularly in a groove in the heavier rear shell (200 mm inner diameter), and two handles let the operator work it. The lower rear shell is welded to a table that supports the device.
problem: A clean, repeatable way to cut aluminum tubing to size was needed without a commercial pipe cutter.
fabcity_relevance: A shop-built, bearing-guided tube cutter is the kind of bootstrap machine-tool a fab lab makes to fabricate other things — tooling that begets tooling.

title: Manual bench grinder built from recovered vehicle parts
summary: A hand-cranked tool grinder/sharpener assembled from a ZIL-130 flywheel, bearings and angle iron.
how_it_works: It is built on a base of 1.5-inch angle iron with 4 pillow-block bearings carrying the shaft on which the abrasive emery wheel is mounted. A ZIL-130 flywheel coupled to a bendix from the same vehicle transmits 200-600 rpm to spin the stone for sharpening tools. The parts used to build the machine are all recovered.
problem: A way to sharpen and grind tools was needed without a manufactured bench grinder.
fabcity_relevance: Turning a salvaged truck flywheel and starter gear into a working grinder is a textbook 'scavenge a drivetrain to make a machine tool' move for a resource-constrained workshop.

title: Hand-shaped axe and pick handles from rough wood
summary: Axe (and pick) handles made by hand from a length of hardwood stick using only basic edge tools.
how_it_works: Construction is done manually using a 90 cm length of round hardwood ('strong stick'), which is shaved down with a machete, plane or a fragment of bottle glass until it fits the head. Pick handles are made in the same artisanal workshop following the same procedure.
problem: Manufactured replacement tool handles were unavailable, halting use of axes and picks.
fabcity_relevance: A reminder that the highest-leverage 'fabrication' is sometimes hand-shaping a consumable wear part from local biomaterial — the zero-machine baseline a fab lab should still teach.

title: Hand-twisted rope from majagua tree bark fiber
summary: Cordage made by hand from the bast fiber of the majagua tree, harvested near rivers and the coast.
how_it_works: Straight, undamaged majagua trees near rivers and the coast are selected. To free the fibers the wood is beaten with another stick of the same material until it turns 'juicy', then the fibers are sun-dried for three days. They are then woven/twisted by hand, cut to a width of about two centimetres.
problem: Manufactured rope and cordage were scarce, so a local fiber source was needed.
fabcity_relevance: Bast-fiber rope from a local tree is a renewable biomaterial feedstock — relevant to fab labs exploring locally-grown materials in place of imported synthetics.

title: Fly-larvae protein production for pig and poultry feed
title_original: Produccion de larvas para la alimentacion animal
summary: A controlled method of breeding fly larvae on agricultural waste to produce high-protein animal feed.
how_it_works: Roofed beds 3-5 cm high and 1 x 3 m are filled with a substrate of ground rice husk (for pigs) or ground cane/bagasse (for poultry and pigs) and moistened to medium humidity. Fly attractants — fish waste, small amounts of cane juice, eggshells or rotted ones, blood mixed with water, and whey — are sprinkled on, and the bed is turned twice daily so it doesn't compact. At 72 hours the larvae must be collected before they turn into flies; fed directly they are up to 63% protein, or 28-33% after drying through a mill.
problem: Imported protein-rich animal feed disappeared, threatening pig and poultry production.
fabcity_relevance: Insect-protein bioconversion of food and farm waste prefigures today's circular-economy feed systems and is buildable at neighborhood scale with no high tech.

title: Cacao-pod husk milled into animal feed
title_original: Cascara del fruto del cacao en la alimentacion
summary: An animal feed ingredient produced by drying and milling cacao-fruit husks, a processing byproduct.
how_it_works: Cacao fruit husks are sun-dried on a cement patio at 30 kg per square metre until they reach 12-15% moisture, then milled to particles under 2 mm in a hammer mill. The resulting product runs about 13.5% moisture, 32% crude fibre and 7.85% crude protein, and can be fed safely to all animal species within inclusion limits of 40% for cattle, 25% for pigs and 10% for poultry.
problem: Conventional feed was scarce, while cacao processing discarded large volumes of husk.
fabcity_relevance: Valorizing an agro-industrial waste stream into a quantified, spec'd feed ingredient is a clean template for local byproduct-to-product loops a fab city can map and operate.

title: Fresh cane juice (guarapo) as on-site pig feed
title_original: Guarapo para la alimentacion del ganado porcino
summary: Sugarcane juice pressed on-site to replace commercial pig feed, supplemented with farm residues.
how_it_works: Guarapo extracted directly from sugarcane substitutes for the commercial feed used in pig-raising, notably increasing the pigs' weight. A cane mill (trapiche) is built right next to the animal pens; cane is brought there and 2-3 workers operate the mill and processing unit. Agricultural residues such as purge molasses, sweet-potato vine and banana stem are also used, and the animals are fed twice a day.
problem: Manufactured pig feed was unavailable, but sugarcane and farm residues were locally abundant.
fabcity_relevance: Co-locating a simple cane press with the livestock to feed them from local crop output is a distributed, short-loop food-production pattern a fab city can replicate.

title: Multi-nutritional molasses-lime blocks for cattle
summary: Large set 'lick' blocks of molasses, lime and additives that supplement cattle on poor diets or needing treatment.
how_it_works: The blocks are a supplementary feed for cattle on low-quality diets or requiring medicinal treatment. The principle is the setting (curing) of mixtures of fine molasses, slaked lime and other additives, with the additive mix determined by technicians and engineers according to the herd's purpose and requirements. Each block or bale reaches roughly 250 kg.
problem: Balanced cattle feed and supplements were scarce, especially for animals on poor forage or needing treatment.
fabcity_relevance: A tunable supplement block formulated to local feedstocks and herd needs shows how a standard product can be re-engineered around whatever inputs a region actually has.

title: Madagascar periwinkle for bovine keratoconjunctivitis
title_original: Tratamiento de la querato conjuntivitis bovina con vicaria blanca
summary: A plant-based veterinary remedy: macerated Madagascar periwinkle applied to treat pinkeye in cattle.
how_it_works: The plant (vicaria blanca / Madagascar periwinkle) is macerated and applied to the animal's eyes to treat bovine keratoconjunctivitis.
problem: Veterinary pharmaceuticals to treat cattle eye infections were unavailable.
fabcity_relevance: Documented ethnoveterinary substitutions are a knowledge resource for bioregional health systems where a fab city can't (and shouldn't) manufacture its own pharmaceuticals.

title: Guasima bark decoction for cattle blood-parasite disease
title_original: Uso de la guasima en el tratamiento de la hemoparasitosis (babesia y anaplasma)
summary: A boiled guasima-bark decoction dosed to cattle to treat hemoparasitosis (babesia and anaplasma).
how_it_works: Preparation: boil 150-200 grams of guasima bark in one litre of water for 20 minutes. Dose: give the animal 500 ml, one to two times.
problem: Manufactured drugs for tick-borne cattle blood parasites (babesia, anaplasma) were unavailable.
fabcity_relevance: A precise dose-and-prep botanical protocol is the kind of locally-actionable veterinary knowledge a fab city's open repository can preserve and circulate.

title: Masonry poultry incubator fitted to standard hatchery gear
summary: A poultry incubator built from concrete blocks and tile, sized to accept the components of a Universal 55 hatcher.
how_it_works: It is built from 10 cm cement blocks (preferably faced with tile) and a 6 cm-thick concrete slab left with a hole for the damper and bulb. The critical interior dimensions (1.90 m high, 1.60 m wide, 2.16 m long) must match the Universal 55 hatcher so its equipment can be transferred into the masonry unit. A separate 42 x 65 x 5 cm frame holding the damper ring and humidity-extractor motor is cast for the back, and tile thickness must be accounted for when laying blocks so the interior dimensions are preserved.
problem: Manufactured incubator cabinets were unavailable, but the working internals of existing hatchers could be salvaged.
fabcity_relevance: Rebuilding the durable shell of a machine in local masonry around salvaged working internals is a smart hybrid-fabrication strategy when only the precision parts are scarce.

title: Rustic multi-fuel heater/stove
summary: A very simple heater/stove that burns green or dry wood, charcoal, or other combustibles.
how_it_works: Its construction is very simple and it can be fed with green or dry firewood, charcoal, or other combustion sources.
problem: Manufactured stoves and reliable cooking/heating fuel were scarce, demanding a simple fuel-flexible burner.
fabcity_relevance: Fuel-agnostic burner design (burn whatever's at hand) is a resilience principle for distributed energy and cooking hardware a fab lab can prototype cheaply.

title: Hand-powered honey extractor for beekeeping
summary: A man-powered centrifugal honey extractor built from galvanized sheet and machined cast parts.
how_it_works: It is a galvanized sheet-metal tank holding an internal element into which the honeycomb frames are placed; this spins at high speed via a transmission mechanism to fling out the honey. It is made of sheet metal, machined cast parts and welded structures, and the energy that drives it is human force.
problem: Commercial powered honey extractors were unavailable to beekeepers.
fabcity_relevance: A hand-cranked centrifuge from sheet metal and welds is a clean fab-lab build that keeps a local food-production craft (beekeeping) viable off-grid.

title: Automatic fence-staple making machine
summary: A shop-buildable machine that automatically forms fence staples from a roll of wire.
how_it_works: It can be made in any workshop and used by any agricultural enterprise. The operator only has to load the roll of wire; the machine does the rest automatically, turning out finished staples ready for use in building fences.
problem: Manufactured fence staples were unavailable for the fencing needed across farms.
fabcity_relevance: A locally-replicable machine that converts bulk wire into a finished fastener is exactly the 'make the consumable, not import it' capability a fab city distributes.

title: Tilapia 'ham' (fish-meat charcuterie)
summary: A cured, molded 'ham' made from ground tilapia stretched with pork fat, blood and flour.
how_it_works: Ten kg of frozen tilapia ground to 2 mm is mixed with 2 kg diced pork fat, 4 kg pork (or ram) blood corpuscles beaten with salt to prevent clotting, 2 g curing salt (sodium nitrite) for colour, 40 drops of liquid humus to remove fishy odour and taste, and 2 kg wheat or soy flour. The mix is packed in a mold with a thermometer hole and cooked in a bain-marie at 75-80 C for 45 minutes without boiling, then compressed, finished at 90 C+, cooled in the mold and refrigerated.
problem: Conventional pork ham and meat were scarce, while farmed tilapia and slaughter byproducts were available.
fabcity_relevance: Reformulating a familiar product (ham) around locally farmed fish and waste blood is a food-sovereignty playbook for substituting scarce inputs with abundant local ones.

title: Canavalia-bean coffee substitute ('nescafe')
summary: A coffee substitute (or extender) made by roasting dried canavalia (jack) beans like coffee.
how_it_works: Canavalia is a year-round crop (best harvest in the cold season) with white, black and pink bean varieties, the pink being highest-yielding. Once the pods are dry, the beans are shelled and roasted just like coffee in a covered container. It tastes very pleasant taken with milk, and mixing natural coffee with this plant is preferable to extending it with chickpeas because the colour, yield and flavour are superior.
problem: Coffee was scarce and needed to be extended or replaced with a locally grown crop.
fabcity_relevance: A roast-and-brew crop substitution for an import-dependent staple (coffee) is a low-tech food-resilience pattern that maps onto bioregional crop strategies.

title: Mixed pork picadillo stretched with viandas and vegetables
summary: A ground-meat dish that extends pork offcuts and byproducts with starchy roots and vegetables.
how_it_works: Pork loin and lacon (cured shoulder) are deboned and ground with pork byproducts on a medium plate; no salt is added because the cured cuts already contain it. The hash is sauteed in 20 g of fat for 6 minutes, then a creole sauce (onion, pepper, tomato, cumin, dry wine) plus separately-cooked viandas or vegetables are added and cooked 5 more minutes, stretching a small amount of meat with ~580g vegetables and ~1160g of starchy garnish.
problem: Meat was scarce, so small amounts of pork and byproducts had to feed more people.
fabcity_relevance: Recipe-level 'extender' strategies that bulk scarce protein with local starches are a food-system resilience pattern worth cataloguing alongside hardware in a city repository.
